drills.title: Neutral pelvis setup
drills.why: S-posture (an over-arched lower back) switches off your core, loads the lower back, and makes you stand up through the ball. That throws your hands out toward the heel.
steps: Lay a club along your spine. It should touch the back of your head, upper back and tailbone.
If there's a big gap at your lower back, tuck your pelvis slightly (flatten the belt buckle) until the gap closes.
Hinge forward from the hips, keeping that flat back, and let your arms hang.
Do this check before every block of shots.
drills.target: Gap at the lower back no bigger than your hand's thickness.

drills.title: Wall / chair drill
drills.why: When your hips push toward the ball (early extension), your hands get pushed out and you strike the heel. You also add loft, which explains your 22° launch with a 27.5° 7-iron.
steps: Set up with your backside lightly touching a wall or a chair back.
Make slow half swings. Keep your trail glute on the wall at the top.
Through impact, your lead glute should slide back to the wall, not away from it.
10 slow reps, then 5 real shots at 60% speed.

videos.title: How to stop early extension and heel strikes

drills.title: Heel gate for driver and woods
drills.why: Session 2 confirmed it: once you centred contact, driver ball speed rose 5 mph and the 3-hybrid and 7-wood carried about 13 yd further. Heel and hosel hits are your biggest leak with the long clubs.
steps: Spray the driver face with foot powder so every strike leaves a mark.
Push a tee into the mat just inside the ball (the heel side), about a clubhead-width away.
Address the ball off the toe-side of the face, the "clubhead closer to you" feel that worked in Session 2.
Swing at 80% and miss the tee. Check the mark after every shot: it should sit in the middle or slightly toward the toe.

videos.title: How to stop hitting the driver out of the heel
Why not to start with the club behind the ball

drills.search: stop hitting driver off the heel drill

drills.title: Towel drill: ball-first compression
drills.why: Carry follows smash closely, and in Session 2 you swung the 7-iron 9 mph harder than Session 1 but got less ball speed (smash 1.28 → 1.13). Effort is costing you contact.
steps: Lay a towel flat 4–6 in. behind the ball.
Swing at 70% and hit the ball without touching the towel, so the low point is ahead of the ball.
Feel your hands ahead of the ball at impact: lead wrist flat, not cupped.
Speed ladder: 5 balls at 60%, 5 at 80%, 5 at 100%. Keep the effort that gives the best smash, not the most club speed.
drills.target: 7-iron smash 1.25+ at about 80% effort, launch under 20°.

videos.title: Towel drill: divot in front of the ball

drills.title: Heel-gate two-ball drill
drills.why: Low smash is where your distance goes. Off-centre (likely heel) contact is one cause; spray the face to see where you're actually hitting it.
steps: Spray the clubface with foot powder spray so every strike leaves a mark.
Place a second ball 1 in. inside the target ball (on the side closest to your feet).
Hit the outer ball without touching the inner one.
Check the face mark and the sim's smash after every shot.

videos.title: Stop hitting the ball off the heel
How to stop hitting heel shots

drills.search: stop hitting heel irons drill two ball

drills.title: Driver face control
drills.why: Your driver path is nearly neutral (−1.7°) but the face is +3.7° open to the target, so drives start right and curve further right (57 yd on average). Unlike your irons, the driver is a face problem.
steps: Check your grip: at address you should see two to three knuckles on your lead hand.
Make slow half swings feeling the toe rotate past the heel through impact (the screwdriver turn).
Hit 5 drivers at 70% and watch face-to-target on the sim: aim for 0 to +1°.
Until it holds, aim 30–40 yd left of target on the course.
drills.target: Driver face-to-target under +1°, average finish within 25 yd.

videos.title: Fix your slice with the Screwdriver Drill
Open clubface at impact: drill to stop the slice

drills.title: Path tidy-up (optional)
drills.why: Your fade is consistent, so it's playable as-is. Trimming the path from −9° toward −5° should still add a few yards, since less out-to-in swings carried a little further.
steps: Put a headcover 2 in. outside the ball and 4–6 in. behind it.
Pull your trail foot back 2–3 in. (slightly closed stance).
Start the downswing by turning your hips first, then swing out toward right field. Miss the headcover.
Check the sim: path −5° or better before you add speed.
drills.target: Path around −5° while keeping the same aim.

videos.title: 3 drills to fix an over-the-top swing

drills.search: headcover drill over the top golf

drills.title: Play the shot you have (DECADE)
drills.why: DECADE is course management, not a swing fix, but it saves strokes right now. Aim for your real dispersion instead of the flag.
steps: Until the path fix holds, aim left of target and let the fade work back.
Aim off your average finish with each club (the Finish column on the Session tab), e.g. if your 8-iron finishes 18 yd right, aim about 18 yd left.
On long par 3s, play to the fat side of the green, not at the pin.
drills.target: More greens hit, fewer short-sided misses.

videos.title: Mastering golf strategy with DECADE: Scott Fawcett

principles.t: Block to learn, mix to keep
principles.b: Work on one change with one club for 20–30 balls, then switch club or shot every ball. Mixed practice feels worse while you do it but holds up better a week later.
principles.src: Golf putting and chipping trials on random vs blocked practice

principles.b: Record everything after the warm-up and judge yourself on the average, not the best. Your best 7-iron isn't your 7-iron; the average is what you'll hit on the course. Only sensor errors and clear tops get excluded.
principles.src: Practical Golf: best vs average shot

principles.b: Scratch players put twice as many balls into the sand and lob wedges as 20+ handicaps (14% vs 7%) and fewer into woods, hybrids and mid irons (42% vs 52%). Aim for about a third wedges, a third irons, a third woods per session; never two long clubs in a row.

principles.t: Change the shot, not just the club
principles.b: Hit the same wedge low and high, short and full. Varying the shot helped higher handicaps most in a pitching study.
principles.src: Differential learning in pitching by handicap (2022)

principles.b: In the mix and test blocks, focus on the target or the strike (ball first, centre of the face), not your arms or hips. Save body cues for the drill block.
principles.src: Wulf & Su, 2007: external focus improved pitch accuracy

principles.b: Better players don't practise longer; their sessions use fewer clubs with a clear purpose. Keep the drill block to one or two clubs and one focus, and write the focus down.
After each week, note one weakness, one strength and one focus for next week in the weekly review box below.
